sections.heading: How to Play Subtlety
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Subtlety"][color=c4]Subtlety Rogue Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]

The rotation for Subtlety Rogue is based on cooldowns combined with two resources you need to manage. The basis is a builder-and-spender system, where combo point builders generate combo points. Finishers are used to consume these combo points when close to the maximum amount (6 or 7 combo points). Energy is the limiting resource most of the time, and it's completely normal to feel resource-starved. Cooldowns allow you to accelerate the cycle and give access to stronger builders, creating a damage profile with serious damage during cooldowns and very low outside.

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
    [tr]
    [td width=6%][icon name=ability_rogue_preparation size=medium type=round color=c4 inline=true][/icon][/td]
    [td][b][color=c4]Resource economy:[/color][/b] Energy and Combo Point income varies a lot on Subtlety; the generation of both resources is low outside of cooldowns but high during. The passive talent [spell=196912] is responsible for a big part of the income; this makes staying within auto attack range essential in both single target and AoE situations. The pacing outside of cooldowns can feel slow as a result.
    [/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
    [tr]
    [td width=6%][icon name=ability_rogue_shadowdance size=medium type=round color=c4 inline=true][/icon][/td]
    [td][b][color=c4]Cooldown Management:[/color][/b] The vast majority of damage is bound to cooldowns, offering Subtlety the unique opportunity to stack them. All cooldowns are aligned to [spell=280719], which means we only use [spell=185313] when the spell is ready. Our major cooldown [spell=121471] is used alongside [spell=185313] when possible, and a second instance of [spell=185313] is typically used right after the first ended (the second cast won't have [spell=280719] ready). Cooldowns don't line up well naturally, which often means we delay both [spell=280719] and [spell=185313] slightly when [spell=121471] is about to come off cooldown.
    [/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
    [tr]
    [td width=6%][icon name=spell_holy_borrowedtime size=medium type=round color=c4 inline=true][/icon][/td]
    [td][b][color=c4]Global Cooldown Efficiency:[/color][/b] All of Subtlety's damage is in Cooldowns, which means utilizing every second becomes essential. Make sure not to cast [spell=185313] during a global cooldown and use your first ability as soon as possible after. This is important because of the [spell=185314] talent, which can extend the duration of [spell=185313] just enough to fit another spell. Any small delay can lead to a loss here. A common strategy to prevent this is the use of a macro that combines the cooldown with a combo point builder or spender.[/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]

[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=ability_stealth type=round size=medium inline=true color=c4][/icon] Best Subtlety Rogue Rotation[/h2]
Subtlety's main priority is managing cooldowns while trying to be resource-efficient. This concentrates as much damage as possible into our cooldown windows. 
The currently [b]recommended Hero talent is [symbol=wow-hero-talent-deathstalker] [color=night-fae]Deathstalker[/color][/b] in all situations. The first week before raid release is a great opportunity to get familiar with the rotation if you haven't played [symbol=wow-hero-talent-deathstalker] [color=night-fae]Deathstalker[/color] before. The hero talent requires slightly closer attention than [symbol=wow-hero-talent-trickster] [color=blizzard-blue]Trickster[/color] due to the high frequency of [spell=457058].

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Subtlety Rogue: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.

sections.heading: Pre-Combat Check Before any combat happens, it is important for Subtlety Rogue to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content. Stealth Always
sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Check[/h2]
    Before any combat happens, it is important for Subtlety Rogue to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.
[center][wrapper width=800px][box]
[ul]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Stealth[/b] [color=q0]Always start combat from [spell=1784].[/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle] [b]Apply Poisons -[/b] [color=q0] Use [b][spell=315584][/b] as your lethal poison and [b][spell=381637][/b] as your utility poison. (Only need to be reapplied if they are about to run out)[/color]
[color=q0][b]The list below highlights the use of each poison:[/b][/color]
[ul]
[li][color=q0]([symbol=d4-poison]Lethal Poison) [spell=315584] - You will almost always want to use this poison for damage.[/color][/li]
[li][color=q0]([symbol=d4-poison]Lethal Poison) [spell=8679] - Can be used in Mythic+ in areas with a lot of mobs with self-healing abilities, like the initial zone in Gambit.[/color][/li]
[li][color=q0]( [symbol=wow-atlas-banker]Utility Poison) [spell=381637] - Is the priority choice in Raiding and Mythic+.[/color][/li]
[li][color=q0]( [symbol=wow-atlas-banker]Utility Poison) [spell=5761] - It is advised to use this instead of [spell=381637] if there is a 2nd rogue in your Raid team to get the benefit of both effects. This poison is also fairly good in Mythic+ in general, and a valid choice and alternative to [spell=381637] in dungeons tanks struggle to survive.[/color][/li]
[li][color=q0]( [symbol=wow-atlas-banker]Utility Poison) [spell=3408] - Is usually not used.[/color][/li]
[/ul]
[/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle](Mythic+ & Raids) [b]Apply Weapon Oils[/b] [color=q0]Use [item=243734] on both weapons. (only need to be re-applied if they are about to run out)[/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle](Mythic+ & Raids) [b]Eat Buff Food and drink Flasks[/b]. (only if you need to reapply them or if the buffs are about to run out)[/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle](Optional) [b]Prepare [spell=470347] Charges -[/b] [color=q0]The first two charges don't reset on encounter or dungeon start; we can exploit this by using [spell=185313] before a pull/key start.[/color][/li]
[/ul]
[/box][/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=rogue][icon name=spell_holy_borrowedtime type=round size=medium inline=true color=c4][/icon] Subtlety Rogue Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2][pad]
Subtlety has access to a variety of different cooldowns. All of them come with some extra wrinkles in how they work rather than simply being flat increases, so the below section covers [i]how[/i] they work, and most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Secret Technique" icon=ability_rogue_sinistercalling]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=rogue] Secret Technique\u200e [/color][/h3]
[spell=280719] is a finishing move that's split into three parts and is the only cooldown on Subtlety that has a static cooldown, which is reduced by haste. The following information is good to know:

[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right]The initial hit deals physical damage, while the second and third hits are shadow damage.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]The Shadow damage attacks count as Clone Attacks; talents interacting with Shadow Clones, like e.g. [spell=382506] typically work with them.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]The Shadow Clone Attacks are minimally delayed.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]The spell is soft target capped at 5 targets (damage reduced to the 6th, 7th, ... target).[/li]
[/ul]
[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=rogue]Optimal Use[/color][/minor-heading]
[div display-options="trickster"]
The optimal use of [spell=280719] is during [spell=185313] as soon as possible. 
[/div]
[div display-options="deathstalker"]
[ul]
[li icon=none][b]Single Target:[/b][/li]
[li][spell=457058] has a higher priority than [spell=280719].[/li]
[li][spell=280719] is still preferably used during [spell=185313].[/li]
[li]You can use [spell=280719] outside of [spell=185313] if you get the cooldown back during the next use of Shadow Dance.[/li]
[li icon=none][b]Multi Target (4+):[/b][/li]
[li]You always want to use [spell=280719] as first or second finisher in [spell=185313] with [spell=1268939].[/li]
[/ul]
[/div]
[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Shadow Dance" icon=ability_rogue_shadowdance]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=rogue]Shadow Dance [/color][/h3]
[spell=185313] is the defining cooldown of Subtlety and allows the use of [spell=1784] specific spells for its duration. Many talents hook into it, passively increasing damage output, the duration, or giving other benefits in addition to that.  The list below highlights some unique aspects:
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right][spell=185313] can't be used while in [spell=1784].[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Macros using [spell=185313] and [spell=185438] at the same time require two button presses to activate [spell=185438].[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][spell=185313] can't be used again while it's up.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][spell=185313] can't be removed with cancelaura.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]The haste interaction from [spell=185314] considers [spell=382505], which means it will extend [spell=185313] for a longer time when under the effect of [spell=382505].[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]The haste interaction from [spell=185314] only works on things increasing your baseline haste. This means effects that increase haste by a % like bloodlust don't work on it, while trinkets that give you a certain amount of haste on use will.[/li]
[/ul]
[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=rogue]Optimal Use[/color][/minor-heading]
[pad]
You always want to use [spell=185313] with either very low combo points or finishing combo points. 
[div display-options="deathstalker"]

The concept is to always empower your [spell=457058] with [spell=1268939]. [spell=457058] should always be used on you as your first or second finishing move in [spell=185313]. (to be also empowered by [spell=470347]) 
This means we use [spell=185313] when [spell=457058] is up or if we have 1 stack of [spell=457052] remaining and [spell=280719] ready.

There is a certain flexibility in [spell=185313] use.

[wrapper width=800px]
[tabs name="deathstalker" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Default" icon=spell_shadow_twilight]
This is the most common case.
[ol]
[li][b][spell=185313] + [spell=197835][/b] [color=q0](or [spell=426591]) -- This should give you [spell=1268939].[/color][/li]
[li][spell=196819][/li]
[li][color=q0](optional)[/color] [spell=185438] [color=q0](only with 5+ stacks of [spell=196912])[/color][/li]
[li][spell=280719][/li]
[/ol]
[b]Note:[/b] You would start this sequence with [spell=457058] up.
[/tab]
[tab name="Apex Up" icon=inv12_apextalent_rogue_ancientarts]
If [spell=1268939] is up; you can adjust your rotation.
[ol]
[li][color=q0] (optional)[/color][spell=426591] [color=q0](if ready)[/color][/li]
[li][spell=185313] + [spell=196819][/li]
[li][color=q0](optional)[/color] [spell=197835] / [spell=185438] [color=q0](only with 5+ stacks of [spell=196912])[/color][/li]
[li][spell=280719][/li]
[/ol]
[b]Note:[/b] You would start this sequence with [spell=1268939] and [spell=457058] up.
[/tab]
[tab name="Stack of Deathstalkers Mark" icon=inv_ability_deathstalkerrogue_deathstalkersmark]
Using [spell=280719] as the first finisher offers additional flexibility and allows cooldowns to be used more quickly.
[ol]
[li][b][spell=185313] + [spell=197835][/b] [color=q0](or [spell=426591])[/color][/li]
[li][spell=280719][/li]
[li][color=q0](optional)[/color] [spell=197835] / [spell=185438] [color=q0](only with 5+ stacks of [spell=196912])[/color][/li]
[li][spell=196819][/li]
[/ol]
[b]Note:[/b] You would start this sequence with 1 stacks of [spell=457052] left.
[/tab]
[tab name="AoE" icon=ability_rogue_sinistercalling]
You always want to use [spell=280719] with [spell=470347](first 2 finishers in Dance) and [spell=1268939] on 4 or more targets.
[ol]
[li][b][spell=185313][/b][/li]
[li][color=q0](optional)[/color] [b][spell=197835][/b] [color=q0](or [spell=426591])[/color][/li]
[li][spell=280719][/li]#secret
[li][color=q0](optional)[/color] [spell=197835] [color=q0](only with 5+ stacks of [spell=196912])[/color][/li]
[li][spell=319175][/li]#bp
[/ol]
[b]Note:[/b] You want to start the sequence with 2 or more stacks of [spell=457052] left. It does not matter what combo points amount you start Dance with.
[/tab]
[/tabs]
[/wrapper]

Additional Tips:[ul]
[li]You typically want to prepare 5+ stacks of [spell=196912], can do so by not using finishing moves shortly before the use of [spell=185313].[/li]
[li]Your second [spell=185313] cast during [spell=121471] is without [spell=280719].[/li]
[li]You can use [spell=1856] - [spell=185438] - [spell=185313] to get to lower [spell=457052] stacks, to avoid or reduce delays of cooldowns.[/li]
[li]It is advised not to use [spell=185313] when [spell=121471] has less than 10 seconds remaining to ensure two casts when it's ready.[/li]
[/ul]

This changes when we fight 4 or more targets. You want to always empower [spell=280719] with [spell=1268939] and use [spell=457058] before [spell=185313].

[/div]
[div display-options="trickster"]
[ul]
[li][symbol=wow-hero-talent-trickster] [color=blizzard-blue]Trickster[/color] - Prefers to start [spell=185313] with finishing combo points.[/li]
[/ul]
Only use it if [spell=280719] is ready (not on cooldown).
Your 2nd [spell=185313] cast during [spell=121471] is used even when [spell=280719] is not ready.
It is advised not to use [spell=185313] when [spell=121471] has less than 10 seconds remaining to ensure two casts when it's ready.

You can prepare [spell=1268939] for your [spell=185313] by not using finishing shortly (up to 5 seconds) before your [spell=280719] comes off cooldown.
[/div]
[pad]

[/tab]
[tab name="Shadow Blades" icon=inv_knife_1h_grimbatolraid_d_03]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=rogue]Shadow Blades[/color][/h3]

[spell=121471] is a 90-second cooldown that doubles the combo point generation of your combo point-building spells. It also echoes 20% of the damage done by spells used during its uptime as shadow damage. The list below lists some additional facts about the spell that might be relevant.

[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right]The cooldown of [spell=121471] is reset with encounters.[/li]
[/ul]
[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=rogue]Optimal Use[/color][/minor-heading]
[pad]
Use with [spell=121471] and [spell=185313].
[pad]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c4][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c4][/icon] Subtlety Rogue Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]
This section talks about optional ways to increase your damage or reliability. You don't need to do these optimizations when learning, but you might want to take a look once you feel comfortable with the rotation basics.
[pad]
[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Global cooldown efficiency" icon=ability_racial_timeismoney]
    [h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c4] The haste problem, and how to solve it.[/color][/h3]

    [spell=185314] increases the duration of [spell=185313] based on your haste value; the amount of extra time can be very low, making it important to use spells as soon as possible. 

    The following is advised in order to minimize impact:
    [ul]
    [li][b]As [symbol=wow-hero-talent-trickster] [color=blizzard-blue]Trickster[/color]:[/b] Use a macro with [spell=280719] and [spell=185313].[/li]
    [li][b]As [symbol=wow-hero-talent-deathstalker] [color=night-fae]Deathstalker[/color]:[/b] Use a macro with [spell=197835] and [spell=185313]. [span class=tip tooltip=macro_s][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
    [li][b]General:[/b] Don't use [spell=185313] during a Global Cooldown.[/li]
    [/ul]

    You can find this and other macros in [symbol=wow-atlas-class][u][url guide=3222 hash=macros]the macro and ui guide[/url][/u].
    
[/tab]
[tab name="Apex Talents" icon=inv12_apextalent_rogue_ancientarts]
    [h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c4] Apex talents.[/color][/h3]
The apex talents increase damage during cooldowns even more, which leads to optimizations that don't seem intuitive. 

[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=rogue]Optimizations[/color][/minor-heading]

The table below highlights optimizations:
[ul]
[li]You can stop using finishing moves a few seconds before [spell=280719] comes off cooldown. [span class=tip tooltip=noattack][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li]Both Hero talents want to optimize around [spell=1268939] [b]during [spell=185313][/b]. This can mean using [spell=185438] or [spell=197835] on high combo points to activate the effect if it's not up for your supercharged finishers.[/li]
[/ul]
[div display-options="trickster"]
Try to have your supercharged finishers empowered by [spell=1268939]. You can prepare for it as highlighted above.
[/div]
[div display-options="deathstalker"]
You already play around this correctly if you prepare your [spell=185313] as outlined in the cooldown section. If you have 5 or more stacks of [spell=196912] can apex your [spell=280719] cast too.
[/div]
[/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad]

Our Subtlety Rogue guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Subtlety Rogue guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].

[tooltip name=NotesHighlight][color=q]Notes will appear here.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=stealth][color=q][spell=185438] is always used from [spell=1784] or [spell=1856]. [spell=185438] teleports you to the target if used this way. This is handy when you want to close the gap to a new pack in Mythic+ faster.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=secret][color=q][spell=280719] is your top priority finisher during [spell=185313] and used as soon as possible.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=dance_d][color=q]Low combo points more specifically refers to one or fewer. You can use [spell=185313] with your high combo points (6 or 7) to finish immediately after, but low combo points are typically better. This spell is your central cooldown, and sensitive to input lag, so make sure not to use it during a global cooldown to be able to fill every global possible.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=dance_t][color=q]You usually want to use [spell=185313] with your high combo points (6 or 7) to finish immediately after, but low combo points (0 or 1) are fine too. This spell is your central cooldown, and sensitive to input lag, so make sure not to use it during a global cooldown to be able to fill every global possible.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=dn][color=q]This is a fall back option to re-apply [spell=457052], which is typically done with [spell=185438]. The use of [spell=196819] is rare as a consequence, making this mostly relevant for pulls that last longer or sustained AoE.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=macro_d][color=q]The use of [spell=185438] would be ideal, but it does not work in a macro now. This introduces a short delay between [spell=185313] and the cast of [spell=185313]. The delay is dependent on your latency and is at least 100ms. This is enough to make [spell=197835] a good alternative. [spell=197835] gets empowered by [spell=185313](200% damage) ,[spell=385722](100% chance to critical hit), procs [spell=382528] and generates full combo points thanks to [spell=343160]. This combination allows it to be close enough in output to use the macro for reliability.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=macro_t][color=q]When using this macro, always make sure to be on 6 or 7 combo points before using [spell=185313]. It is better to stop using finishers ~3-4 seconds before [spell=280719] comes off cooldown than to delay the use of the macro.[/color][/tooltip]
